messages.author: 9600a7a9e426959d
messages.subject: commonfactorGWAS resulting in 50K SNPs
parts:
My commonfactorGWAS only resulted in over 50K SNPs. Is this okay? I generally observe >1million SNPs at the end of the commonfactorGWAS.

One of the reasons could be that one of the 6 traits of my multivariate GWAS had only 480,000 SNPs at the beginning and after munging had only 50K SNPs. But I am not sure if this has normally been observed.

Your feedback will be very useful.

Best regards,
Rajini

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: commonfactorGWAS resulting in 50K SNPs
parts:
Hi Rajini, 

Apologies for late reply. I would say the 50k SNPs makes sense given a trait with only 480k SNPs, but I would not personally use any traits with <  1 million SNPs. As long as the 480k SNPs are a random sampling of the genome (e.g., not just the top 480k SNPs from a GWAS), then results are still likely to be trustworthy as far as the 50k SNPs you are getting results. That being said, your genomic coverage with 50k SNPs is so poor I would vote to exclude the sixth trait with only the 480k to begin with. 

Best, 
  Andrew
